title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
abstract: arXiv:2611.07948v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, evaluating the correctness of their responses is crucial for reliable use. However, such evaluation is challenging because reference answers are rarely available in practice. Existing reference-free methods mainly rely on output signals, which may assign high scores to incorrect responses and thus do not necessarily reflect correctness. This motivates exploring the model's internal computation for complementary correctness signals. Recent studies exploit internal states, but they mainly analyze hidden-state trajectories across layers, which record only the combined updates of attention and feed-forward networks (FFNs) and overlook how these components interact. We therefore propose Circe, a training-free self-evaluation method that assesses a response using both internal and external signals, without reference answers or repeated sampling. For internal

translated_title: Circe：基于组件交互一致性的免训练大语言模型自我评估方法
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型在实际应用中的部署日益增多，评估其回答的正确性对于可靠使用至关重要。然而，这种评估具有挑战性，因为在实践中参考答案往往难以获得。现有的免参考方法主要依赖输出信号，这可能会给错误的回答赋予高分，因此并不一定能反映正确性。这促使我们探索模型内部计算以获取互补的正确性信号。近期研究利用了内部状态，但它们主要分析跨层的隐藏状态轨迹，这仅记录了注意力机制和前馈网络（FFN）的组合更新，而忽视了这些组件之间如何交互。因此，我们提出了Circe，一种免训练的自我评估方法，它结合内部和外部信号来评估回答，无需参考答案或重复采样。对于内部
tldr: 提出Circe——一种免训练的大语言模型自我评估方法，通过分析注意力与前馈网络等组件间的交互一致性并结合内外部信号来评估回答正确性，无需参考答案或重复采样。
en_tdlr: Circe is a training-free LLM self-evaluation method that assesses response correctness by exploiting component interaction consistency (e.g., attention and FFN interactions) alongside internal and external signals, without requiring reference answers or repeated sampling.
